peptide.name: CJC-1295 (with DAC)
peptide.summary: CJC-1295 with DAC is a long-acting analog of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) fragment (1-29), chemically modified with a Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) that covalently binds circulating albumin. This extends its half-life from minutes to approximately 6-8 days, allowing once- or twice-weekly dosing with sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation. It is a distinct entry from CJC-1295 (no DAC) / Modified GRF(1-29), which shares the same peptide backbone but clears in about 30 minutes.
peptide.description: CJC-1295 is built on the same tetrasubstituted GHRH(1-29) backbone as the no-DAC (Modified GRF) version, but carries an added maleimidopropionyl-linked DAC group. After subcutaneous injection, the maleimide reacts with the free thiol on cysteine-34 of circulating albumin, forming a stable covalent thioether bond. Because albumin itself has a plasma half-life of roughly 19 days, this conjugation shields the peptide from renal filtration and proteolytic clearance, extending its own half-life to about 6-8 days. A single dose has been shown in a phase I randomized, placebo-controlled trial (Teichman et al., 2006) to produce dose-dependent 2- to 10-fold GH elevations and 1.5- to 3-fold IGF-1 elevations lasting 9-11 days; with repeated dosing, IGF-1 remained elevated for up to 28 days. It is not FDA-approved and has no approved clinical indication; it is sold as a research chemical.
peptide.mechanism_of_action: Binds the GHRH receptor (GHRHR) on pituitary somatotrophs to stimulate GH synthesis and release, identical in principle to the no-DAC form. The DAC modification covalently conjugates the peptide to serum albumin via cysteine-34, adopting albumin's slow clearance kinetics and converting a normally pulsatile, short-acting GHRH signal into a sustained, days-long elevation of GH and downstream IGF-1.

half_life.note: Approximately 6-8 days due to covalent albumin conjugation via the DAC group. Contrast with CJC-1295 (no DAC), which has a half-life of about 30 minutes.

peptide.evidence_note: A phase I randomized, placebo-controlled human trial (Teichman 2006) characterized dose-dependent GH/IGF-1 elevation and pharmacokinetics. No trials have established efficacy for the marketed body-composition or anti-aging uses, and there is no approved indication.
peptide.fda_status_note: Not FDA-approved for any indication. Sold by research-chemical vendors 'for research use only,' which does not authorize human use.
peptide.compounding_note: Not an FDA-approved drug, no USP monograph, not on the 503A bulks list; not eligible for legal pharmacy compounding. GHRH-analog peptides broadly were affected by FDA compounding restrictions beginning around 2023-2024.

benefits.label: Sustained GH elevation (early-human)
benefits.detail: A single dose produced 2- to 10-fold GH elevation for 6+ days in a controlled human trial.

benefits.label: Sustained IGF-1 elevation (early-human)
benefits.detail: 1.5- to 3-fold IGF-1 elevation lasting 9-11 days after a single dose; elevated up to 28 days with repeat dosing.

benefits.label: Body composition / recovery (marketed, low evidence)
benefits.detail: Marketed for lean mass, fat loss, sleep, and recovery; not supported by high-quality human outcome trials.

risks.label: GH-axis effects
risks.detail: Sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation carries theoretical risks (insulin resistance, fluid retention, effects on occult tumors) over a much longer window than short-acting secretagogues.

risks.label: Unestablished long-term safety
risks.detail: No long-term human safety data for the marketed uses; the phase I trial was short-term and dose-finding.

contraindications.label: Competitive athletes
contraindications.detail: GHRH analogs / GH secretagogues are prohibited under WADA S2.

contraindications.label: Active malignancy
contraindications.detail: Sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation; avoid pending data.

reconstitution.note: Lyophilized powder reconstituted with bacteriostatic water; final concentration depends on diluent volume. Due to the long half-life, dosing frequency is much lower than the no-DAC form.

lyophilized.stability: Stable when kept cold and dry.

reconstituted.stability: Refrigerate; use within a limited window.

peptide.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. CJC-1295 (with DAC) is not FDA-approved and is prohibited in sport. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

dose_ranges.context: Commonly cited non-clinical use range — NOT validated
dose_ranges.note: Frequently reported anecdotal range, dosed weekly due to the long half-life. No controlled trial validates this specific range or frequency for non-clinical goals. Documented for reference only; not a recommendation.

dose_ranges.context: Phase I trial dose-finding range (reference, not a human-use recommendation)
dose_ranges.note: The Teichman 2006 trial tested single doses of 1-30 mcg/kg to characterize the dose-response relationship, not a repeat-dosing regimen.

protocols.name: Weekly/twice-weekly dosing (anecdotal pattern)
protocols.description: Non-clinical sources describe once- or twice-weekly subcutaneous dosing, leveraging the long half-life for sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation between injections. Summarized only to document the reported pattern.
protocols.cycling_notes: No validated cycling protocol exists in humans.
protocols.disclaimer: Informational summary of anecdotal usage. Not medical advice or a dosing recommendation.

related.note: Same GHRH(1-29) peptide backbone; CJC-1295 with DAC is albumin-conjugated for a ~6-8 day half-life, while the no-DAC form clears in about 30 minutes and preserves pulsatile release.
GHRH analog sometimes paired with the selective GHS ipamorelin, though the short-acting no-DAC form is more commonly used for this pairing.
